title: FBR POS for Restaurants in Pakistan: A 2026 Setup Guide
metaDescription: How restaurants in Pakistan integrate an FBR POS system in 2026 — dine-in vs takeaway, service charge, peak-hour volume, and the IRIS settings that matter.
content:
What FBR POS integration means for a restaurant

An FBR POS system for a restaurant is software that reports every dine-in, takeaway, and delivery sale to the Federal Board of Revenue in real time and prints a QR-coded invoice the customer can verify. For food businesses the challenge is not the law itself but the pace: high order volume, frequent modifications, and split bills all have to flow to FBR IRIS without slowing service.

Restaurants are squarely in FBR's enforcement focus, and a busy outlet that under-reports — even by accident — can face penalties from PKR 10,000 into the hundreds of thousands. Getting the setup right once saves a great deal of trouble later.

Where restaurants differ from retail

A shop sells discrete items; a restaurant sells an evolving order. Items get added mid-meal, orders get split across guests, service charge is applied, and tables turn over fast. Your POS has to keep the FBR invoice in step with all of that and only finalise the reported invoice when the bill is settled, not when the first item is rung in.

Setting it up the right way

  1. Confirm your STRN is active on the IRIS portal before anything else.
  2. Map your menu to correct tax rates — many F&B items carry specific rates, and applying a flat rate to everything is a frequent error.
  3. Decide invoice timing — generate the reported invoice at bill settlement, after all modifications.
  4. Configure the kitchen flow so KDS tickets and the FBR invoice stay linked to the same order.
  5. Run five test bills — one dine-in, one takeaway, one split, one void, one with service charge — and confirm each appears correctly in IRIS.
  6. Set up offline queueing so a connectivity drop never blocks billing.

A real example: a Lahore cafe

A mid-sized cafe in Gulberg, Lahore went live without testing voids. Cancelled orders were deleted on the POS but still sat in IRIS as valid invoices. Within a month the reported sales were thousands of rupees higher than actual revenue, and untangling it took an accountant two days. After fixing the void-reporting setting and adding a monthly reconciliation, the discrepancy disappeared.

Common mistakes restaurants make

  • Treating takeaway and delivery as exempt from invoicing — they are not.
  • Applying one tax rate to the whole menu instead of mapping items correctly.
  • Voiding orders locally without reporting the cancellation to IRIS.
  • No offline queue, so the POS stalls during peak-hour outages.

Keeping it compliant after go-live

Reconcile your POS sales against the IRIS dashboard every month, keep the software updated as FBR rules change, and review your menu's tax mapping whenever rates are revised. For the broader routine, our FBR compliance checklist lays out the full monthly process, and if you hit submission errors the guide to common FBR POS issues and fixes covers the usual culprits.

faqs.question: Do takeaway and delivery orders need FBR invoices too?
faqs.answer: Yes. Every taxable sale — dine-in, takeaway, or delivery — must generate an FBR-reported, QR-coded invoice. Delivery orders routed through aggregators still need a compliant invoice from your own POS.

faqs.question: How is service charge handled on an FBR invoice?
faqs.answer: Service charge is part of the taxable value unless your tax advisor confirms otherwise, so it must appear on the invoice and be included in what is reported to IRIS. Misclassifying it is a common cause of reconciliation gaps.

faqs.question: Can my restaurant POS keep billing if the internet drops mid-service?
faqs.answer: A compliant POS queues orders locally during an outage and submits them to FBR IRIS with their original timestamps once the connection returns, so a Friday-night rush is never blocked by connectivity.

faqs.question: What happens if a waiter voids an order after the invoice is generated?
faqs.answer: Voids and modifications must be recorded and reported, not just deleted locally. An invoice that exists in IRIS but was cancelled only on the POS creates a discrepancy FBR can flag.
